title: Filtered prelog pushouts with varying monoids and rings
statement:
Let $I$ be a small filtered category (nonempty, with common targets for pairs of objects and eventual equalizers of parallel arrows), in a universe containing all sets below [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $M_i$ be a functor from $I$ to commutative monoids and $B_i$ a functor to commutative unital rings, with compatible monoid homomorphisms $\gamma_i:M_i\to(B_i,\cdot)$. Write $M=\varinjlim_iM_i$ and $B=\varinjlim_iB_i$ for their colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], with induced $\gamma:M\to(B,\cdot)$. Put $E_i=\gamma_i^{-1}(B_i^\times)$ and $E=\gamma^{-1}(B^\times)$. Define $Q_i$ as the commutative-monoid quotient of $M_i\times B_i^\times$ by the congruence generated by $(me,u)\sim(m,\gamma_i(e)u)$ for $e\in E_i$, and define $Q=M\oplus_E B^\times$ by the identical presentation. The canonical map
$$\varinjlim_i |Q_i|\longrightarrow Q,\qquad [[m_i,u_i]]\longmapsto[\iota_i(m_i),b_i(u_i)]$$
is bijective, and is a monoid isomorphism when the set colimit is equipped with multiplication at common stages. It respects the structural maps to $B$, the maps from all $M_i$ and $B_i^\times$, and is natural under compatible morphisms of the diagrams. No cancellation, finite generation, or injectivity of transition maps is assumed.

proof.text: A compatible prelog map sends each generator (p,1)~(1,a) to the target generator (h(p),1)~(1,r(a)). The generated congruence is therefore contained in the kernel of the pair map followed by the target quotient. Lift it to the quotient to define the transition maps. Identity, composition, and cocone naturality follow on pair representatives. The map (p,a) ↦ γ(p)a also annihilates each generator, giving the structural map. The colimit factorization gives prelogColimitMap_ι.

source.place: Tag 04AX, section-directed-colimits, eventual equality following Definition 002V (definition-directed); agent-written inverse for varying prelog unit pushouts. Lean realization by Y3: universal-property construction of the inverse using the separate monoid and unit colimits.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise] to represent the inverse of a ring element whose colimit image is a unit. Move both elements to a common stage. Their product equals one eventually; the same-stage equality criterion of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] supplies one arrow along which the product is one. Commutativity supplies the inverse equation in the other order. Thus an element becomes a unit after an arrow from its prescribed stage. Every limiting unit consequently has a stage unit representative. Equality of two units is equality of their values; the same-stage eventual-equality criterion for the ring colimit gives the corresponding criterion for units. The elementwise colimit criterion therefore exhibits the units of the ring colimit as the colimit of the stage unit monoids.

proof.text: For any cocone s on the stage quotient monoids, compose its legs with m↦[m,1] to obtain a cocone on M_i, and with a↦[1,a] to obtain a cocone on the unit monoids. Their colimit universal properties [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] give monoid homomorphisms f:M→s and g:B^×→s. Their coproduct H(m,a)=f(m)g(a) is a monoid homomorphism, and H(ι_i(m),b_i(a))=s_i([m,a]) because [m,1][1,a]=[m,a]. Independence and multiplicativity are built into these universal properties.

source.place: Tag 04AX, section-directed-colimits, eventual equality following Definition 002V (definition-directed); agent-written inverse for varying prelog unit pushouts. Lean realization by Y3: universal-property construction of the inverse using the separate monoid and unit colimits.

proof.text: For a final generator (p,1)~(1,a) with γ(p)=a, use [lem-trf-commutative-monoid-filtered-colimit-underlying] to represent p by m_i. Step 2 gives a transition to j where γ_j(m_j) is the value of a unit b_j. Compatibility shows that b_j maps to a. The formula of Step 3 identifies H(p,1) and H(1,a) with s_j([m_j,1]) and s_j([1,b_j]); these are equal by the stage generator. Hence H descends through the generated congruence to a monoid map Q→s. Its composite with every stage leg is s_i, as checked on pair representatives.

source.place: Tag 04AX, section-directed-colimits, eventual equality following Definition 002V (definition-directed); agent-written inverse for varying prelog unit pushouts. Lean realization by Y3: universal-property construction of the inverse using the separate monoid and unit colimits.

proof.text: Two maps from Q agreeing on its stage legs agree on [p,1], by a stage representative of p, and on [1,a], by a stage representative of the unit a. They agree on every [p,a]=[p,1][1,a], hence everywhere. This gives the uniqueness required by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], proving that the canonical cocone to Q is colimiting in commutative monoids. By [lem-trf-commutative-monoid-filtered-colimit-underlying], its underlying cocone is colimiting in sets. Uniqueness of colimits identifies its canonical comparison from the specified chosen set colimit with an isomorphism, so that comparison is bijective.

source.place: Tag 04AX, section-directed-colimits, eventual equality following Definition 002V (definition-directed); agent-written inverse for varying prelog unit pushouts. Lean realization by Y3: universal-property construction of the inverse using the separate monoid and unit colimits.

proof.text: Transport the commutative monoid structure of Q along the bijective canonical comparison. Apply its injectivity to check the common-stage multiplication formula: the comparison sends each coprojection to the corresponding monoid cocone leg, which is multiplicative, and the cocone laws identify both common-stage images. The identity formula follows from preservation of one by a leg. The resulting multiplicative equivalence has exactly the canonical comparison as its underlying function. The representative formula is colimit.ι_desc. The structural formula follows from prelogColimitMap_ι and the multiplicativity of the ring coprojection. For naturality of the induced prelog map, test on each monoid coprojection and use the two prescribed induced-map identities. For naturality of the quotient comparison, reduce to a pair representative and apply those same identities to its monoid coordinate and unit value. These arguments include reindexing and use no cancellation, finiteness or injectivity assumptions.
